ds: Schemes in which criminals lend their own illicit funds to themselves or their entities through apparently legitimate loans, or send funds abroad and return them as investment, loans or trade receipts. Documentation creates a credible-looking origin for the money.

src.t: FATF, Money Laundering Typologies: loan-back schemes (general)
FATF and Egmont Group, Concealment of Beneficial Ownership (2018)
JMLSG Guidance, lending and sector guidance (general)

cn.rt: Self-lending and rapid or third-party loan repayment, or term deposit collateral, to give funds a lawful-looking origin.

rat: Self-funded loans, cash-collateralised lending and offshore round-tripping.

ind.n: Loan funded by related offshore party and repaid early
ind.cx: Borrower receives loan from an entity linked to themselves and repays rapidly.
ind.ds: Borrower receives loan from an entity linked to themselves and repays rapidly.

ind.n: Loan secured on assets or deposits from third parties of unclear origin
ind.cx: Collateral is cash deposit or asset funded by unknown source.
ind.ds: Collateral is cash deposit or asset funded by unknown source.

ind.n: Funds return from offshore as foreign investment
ind.cx: Money sent abroad reappears as shareholder investment or loan.
ind.ds: Money sent abroad reappears as shareholder investment or loan.

ind.n: Loan with no commercial purpose or unusual terms
ind.cx: Interest-free, no repayments, or terms inconsistent with market.
ind.ds: Interest-free, no repayments, or terms inconsistent with market.

ind.n: Inconsistent loan documentation or backdated agreements
Borrower repays from unrelated third-party sources
ind.ds: Funds are paid or received, or instructions are given to pay, through parties with no evident link to the customer, contract, debt or insured interest. Includes third-party cheques, loan repayments, premiums, gaming funds and goods payments not matching the documentation.
ind.cn: Payments from or to unrelated third parties

ind.n: Customer indifferent to cost of credit
ind.ds: Customer readily accepts poor terms, fees, losses, penalties or prices, showing little interest in performance, provenance or negotiation.
ind.cn: Customer indifferent to cost, return or value

ind.n: Circular trade or invoices among connected entities
ind.cx: Invoices cycled among related firms, returning funds to origin.
ind.ds: Invoices cycled among related firms, returning funds to origin.

ctl.ds: Detects funds that return to their origin or loop between linked parties through reciprocal, matched, netted or round-trip flows using graph analysis and account comparison. It exposes artificial turnover and loan-back structures.

Independently verifies stated income, employment, obligations and application facts against third-party, bureau and prior-history data at origination. It reduces application, credit and insurance fraud.
Verifies lender ownership, loan terms and rationale, collateral origin and repayment sources, and alerts on early or third-party repayment. It prevents loans being used to place or layer funds.

Caps transaction size, frequency, load, withdrawal and deposit values, with staged increases as legitimate behaviour is established and per-customer limits at kiosks. It bounds the loss and laundering capacity of new or higher-risk accounts.

Obtains and tests documentary evidence of where the money for a transaction, deposit or capital injection comes from, particularly when value exceeds thresholds or the customer profile. It reduces the chance that illicit proceeds are accepted without explanation.

Cross-checks asset ownership, title history, security registrations and registry changes against official registers, including for changes close to designation or transaction dates. It confirms that the person presenting an asset genuinely owns it.

Checks identity and supporting documents for tampering, forgery, template reuse and internal inconsistency, and corroborates their data against authoritative or reliable independent sources. It exposes altered or counterfeit credentials that pass a visual check.

ctl.n: Licence and permit verification for regulated goods
ctl.ds: Validates licences, permits, certificates and authorisations with the issuing authority and compares their scope with observed activity or shipments. It prevents genuine permits being misused or forged permits being accepted.

Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.

ctl.n: Purpose and intended nature of relationship
ctl.ds: Captures and challenges the stated purpose of the account, expected activity, volumes and geographies at onboarding, creating a baseline against which later behaviour is judged. Vague or implausible answers prompt further enquiry or decline.
Tailors training content and frequency to role and risk for finance, relationship, underwriting and compliance staff, with feedback of quality assurance findings. It builds baseline competence.
Links accounts, devices, addresses, directors and beneficiaries to surface rings, shared attributes and flow structures that single-account views miss. It supports detection of organised networks.

Reconciles trade documents, invoices and shipments with the payments that settle them and reviews settlement made outside standard banking channels. It exposes trade-based laundering where payment logic does not match the underlying deal.
